subject: ESS HL

stimulus.title: Climate and productivity in three terrestrial biomes
stimulus.description: Hypothetical long-term mean values for three sites.
stimulus.note: NPP index values are relative; other factors such as soil fertility are not shown.

question: Compare the productivity of the three sites and explain how temperature, precipitation and growing-season length could account for the pattern. State one limitation of the data.
markscheme: Uses the NPP index to rank productivity as A > B > C, with A about 5.5 times the index of C.
Explains that warm temperatures and abundant precipitation at A reduce climatic limitation and support year-round or near year-round photosynthesis.
Explains that low temperature, low precipitation and the short growing season at C strongly limit plant growth and productivity; B is intermediate.
States a valid limitation such as missing soil fertility, disturbance, species composition or measurement uncertainty, so climate alone cannot fully explain NPP.
markschemeJa: NPP indexからproductivityをA>B>Cと比較し、AはCの約5.5倍であると示す。
Aでは高温・多雨によりclimatic limitationが小さく、年間を通じてまたは長期間photosynthesisが可能と説明する。
Cでは低温・少雨・短いgrowing seasonがplant growthとproductivityを強く制限し、Bは中間的と説明する。
soil fertility、disturbance、species composition、measurement uncertaintyなどが不明で、climateだけではNPPを完全に説明できないと述べる。
modelAnswer: Site A has the highest NPP index at 132, followed by B at 78 and C at 24; A is about 5.5 times C. A is warm and wet with a 12-month growing season, allowing sustained photosynthesis. C is cold and dry and has only a three-month growing season, so both temperature and water availability restrict production. B is intermediate. The comparison is incomplete because soil fertility, disturbance and species composition are not provided.
modelAnswerJa: Site AのNPP indexは132で最も高く、Bが78、Cが24で、AはCの約5.5倍です。Aは高温・多雨でgrowing seasonが12か月あり、長期間photosynthesisできます。Cは低温・少雨でgrowing seasonも3か月しかなく、temperatureとwater availabilityの両方がproductionを制限します。Bは中間的です。ただしsoil fertilityやdisturbance、species compositionが不明なので、climateだけで完全には説明できません。

subject: ESS HL
unit: 2.5 Zonation, succession and change in ecosystems
primaryUnit: 2.5 Zonation, succession and change in ecosystems
requiredUnits: 2.5 Zonation, succession and change in ecosystems

stimulus.title: Primary succession on a newly exposed volcanic surface
stimulus.description: Hypothetical measurements from surfaces of different ages after lava cooled.
stimulus.note: Sites are assumed to have similar climate and parent material.

question: Calculate the percentage increase in plant species richness from year 5 to year 120 and explain two processes that could link soil development to the succession pattern shown.
markscheme: Calculates the percentage increase in species richness as ((37 - 3) / 3) × 100 ≈ 1133%.
Explains that pioneer organisms and weathering help create or deepen soil, allowing more plant species to establish.
Explains that litter production and decomposition increase soil organic matter and nutrient availability, improving conditions for later-successional species.
Links increasing soil depth and organic matter with the rise in species richness, while recognizing that succession is driven by interacting biotic and abiotic processes.
markschemeJa: species richnessの増加率を((37−3)÷3)×100≈1133%と計算する。
pioneer organismやweatheringがsoil形成・深さの増加に寄与し、より多くのplant speciesが定着できると説明する。
litterとdecompositionによってsoil organic matterやnutrient availabilityが増え、later-successional speciesに適した条件が形成されると説明する。
soil depth・organic matterの増加とspecies richnessの上昇を結びつけ、successionはbiotic/abiotic processの相互作用で進むと認識する。
modelAnswer: Species richness increases from 3 to 37, an increase of about 1133%. On a new volcanic surface, weathering and pioneer organisms gradually create soil. As plants establish, litter and decomposition add organic matter and nutrients, improving water retention and fertility. These changes allow a wider range of later species to colonize, which is consistent with the increases in soil depth, organic matter and species richness.
modelAnswerJa: species richnessは3から37へ増え、約1133%の増加です。新しい火山表面ではweatheringやpioneer organismによって徐々にsoilが形成されます。plantが定着するとlitterとdecompositionによりorganic matterとnutrientが増え、water retentionやfertilityも改善します。その結果、より多くのlater speciesが定着でき、soil depth・organic matter・species richnessが一緒に増加するpatternと一致します。

subject: ESS HL

stimulus.title: Genetic indicators for three populations of an endangered mammal
stimulus.description: Hypothetical population estimates from the same species.
stimulus.note: Observed heterozygosity is used here as a simplified indicator of genetic diversity.

question: Analyse which population appears most vulnerable to loss of genetic diversity and explain why low genetic diversity can reduce long-term population resilience.
markscheme: Identifies Population Z as most vulnerable because it has the smallest population, fewest breeding adults and lowest heterozygosity.
Links the recent bottleneck and small breeding population to stronger genetic drift and greater loss of alleles.
Explains that low genetic diversity can increase inbreeding and the expression of harmful recessive alleles and/or reduce reproductive fitness.
Explains that reduced genetic variation can limit the capacity to adapt to environmental change, disease or other selective pressures, lowering resilience.
markschemeJa: Population Zはpopulation size・breeding adultsが最小でheterozygosityも最低なため、genetic diversity lossへのvulnerabilityが最も高いと示す。
recent bottleneckと小さいbreeding populationを、強いgenetic driftやallele lossと関連づける。
low genetic diversityはinbreedingやharmful recessive alleleの発現、reproductive fitness低下につながり得ると説明する。
genetic variationが少ないとenvironmental changeやdiseaseなどへのadaptation capacityが低下し、resilienceが弱くなると説明する。
modelAnswer: Population Z is the most vulnerable because it has only 75 individuals, 18 breeding adults and the lowest heterozygosity at 0.24. A recent bottleneck and very small breeding population increase genetic drift and allele loss. Low diversity can increase inbreeding and reduce fitness, and it also leaves fewer genetic variants available for adaptation to disease or environmental change.
modelAnswerJa: Population Zが最も脆弱です。個体数75、breeding adults 18、heterozygosity 0.24でいずれも最も低いからです。recent bottleneckと小さなbreeding populationはgenetic driftとallele lossを強めます。diversityが低いとinbreedingやfitness低下が起こりやすく、diseaseやenvironmental changeへのadaptationに使えるvariationも少なくなります。

subject: ESS HL

stimulus.title: Three management strategies for an invasive shrub
stimulus.description: Hypothetical outcomes after five years in similar reserves.
stimulus.note: Herbicide impacts and long-term funding stability are not quantified.

question: Compare the strategies and evaluate which appears most effective for biodiversity conservation. Include one limitation of the evidence.
markscheme: Uses the data to show that no control has the highest invasive cover and lowest native-richness index, indicating continued biodiversity pressure.
Recognizes that mechanical removal reduces invasive cover and improves native richness but requires repeated labour and has intermediate cost.
Recognizes that targeted removal plus native replanting gives the lowest invasive cover and highest native-richness index but has the highest listed annual cost.
Evaluates the combined strategy as the most ecologically effective in the stated data because it suppresses the invasive species while actively supporting recovery of native vegetation.
States a valid limitation such as lack of long-term data, unmeasured herbicide/non-target impacts, uncertainty about reinvasion, or missing information on funding and other taxa.
markschemeJa: no controlではinvasive coverが最大でnative-richness indexが最低となり、biodiversityへのpressureが継続するとdataから示す。
mechanical removalはinvasive coverを減らしnative richnessを改善するが、repeated labourが必要でcostは中程度と認識する。
targeted removal＋native replantingはinvasive coverが最小、native-richness indexが最大だがannual costも最大と認識する。
示されたdataではinvasive speciesを抑えつつnative vegetationのrecoveryも促すため、combined strategyがecologically最もeffectiveと評価する。
long-term data不足、non-target impact、reinvasion、funding stability、他taxaのdata不足など妥当なlimitを述べる。
modelAnswer: The combined removal-and-replanting strategy performs best ecologically: invasive cover is only 18% and the native-richness index reaches 124. Mechanical removal also improves conditions but leaves more invasive cover and requires repeated labour. No control performs worst. The combined option therefore appears most effective for biodiversity recovery despite its higher cost, although five years is short and reinvasion, non-target effects and long-term funding are not quantified.
modelAnswerJa: ecologicalにはremoval＋replantingが最も良好で、invasive coverは18%、native-richness indexは124です。mechanical removalも改善しますが、invasive coverがより多く残りrepeated labourが必要です。no controlは最も悪い結果です。したがって高costでもcombined optionがbiodiversity recoveryには最もeffectiveに見えますが、5年間だけでは短く、reinvasionやnon-target effect、long-term fundingは不明です。

subject: ESS HL

stimulus.title: Water-management options for City R
stimulus.description: Hypothetical annual values for a city with current demand of 300 million m³ yr⁻¹.
columns: Additional supply or demand reduction (million m³ yr⁻¹)
rows: Depends on behaviour and appliance uptake
stimulus.note: Options can be combined. Current reliable supply is 225 million m³ yr⁻¹.

question: Calculate the current annual water deficit and determine whether leak reduction plus household efficiency would eliminate it. Analyse why a diversified portfolio may be preferable to relying only on desalination.
markscheme: Calculates current deficit as 300 - 225 = 75 million m³ yr⁻¹.
Calculates combined leak reduction plus household efficiency as 35 + 30 = 65 million m³ yr⁻¹ and concludes that a 10 million m³ yr⁻¹ deficit would remain.
Recognizes that desalination alone supplies 70 million m³ yr⁻¹, still slightly below the 75 million m³ deficit under the stated values.
Analyses that reuse and demand-management options have lower energy and cost indices and can reduce pressure on freshwater resources, while desalination may add energy use and brine impacts.
Explains that a diversified portfolio can spread risk, combine supply and demand management, and reduce dependence on one technology whose cost or environmental impact may be high.
markschemeJa: current deficitを300−225＝75 million m³/yrと計算する。
leak reduction＋household efficiencyを35＋30＝65 million m³/yrと計算し、10 million m³/yrのdeficitが残ると結論づける。
desalination単独は70 million m³/yrで、示された75 million m³ deficitをわずかに満たさないと認識する。
reuseやdemand managementはenergy/cost indexが低くfreshwater pressureを減らし得る一方、desalinationはenergy useやbrine impactを伴うと分析する。
diversified portfolioはsupplyとdemand managementを組み合わせ、1つのtechnologyへの依存とriskを減らせると説明する。
modelAnswer: The city has a 75 million m³ annual deficit. Leak reduction and household efficiency together save 65 million m³, so 10 million m³ would still be missing. Desalination alone provides 70 million m³, also just short of the deficit. A portfolio is preferable because lower-energy demand reduction and reuse can reduce pressure at lower cost, while desalination can provide reliable supply but has higher energy use and brine impacts. Combining measures spreads risk and reduces dependence on one solution.
modelAnswerJa: cityのannual deficitは75 million m³です。leak reductionとhousehold efficiencyの合計は65 million m³なので、10 million m³不足が残ります。desalination単独も70 million m³で、わずかに不足します。低energyのdemand reductionやreuseを組み合わせれば低costでpressureを下げられ、desalinationはreliable supplyを補えますがenergy useとbrine impactがあります。portfolio化することで1つのsolutionへの依存を減らせます。

subject: ESS HL

stimulus.title: Nitrogen use in two cereal systems
columns: Nitrogen removed in harvested crop (kg N ha⁻¹)
stimulus.note: Nitrogen-use efficiency (NUE) = crop N removed / N input × 100. Nitrogen surplus = input - crop N removed.

question: Calculate NUE and nitrogen surplus for both systems, compare their performance, and explain one environmental consequence of a large nitrogen surplus.
markscheme: Calculates System A NUE as 105 / 190 × 100 ≈ 55.3% and surplus as 85 kg N ha⁻¹.
Calculates System B NUE as 92 / 135 × 100 ≈ 68.1% and surplus as 43 kg N ha⁻¹.
Compares B as more nitrogen-efficient with a much smaller surplus, while its yield is only 0.5 t ha⁻¹ lower than A.
Uses the soil-organic-matter trend to recognize that B may also be more supportive of long-term soil condition, while noting that other inputs and management are not shown.
Explains one consequence of nitrogen surplus such as nitrate leaching/eutrophication, ammonia loss, nitrous oxide emissions or soil/water-quality degradation.
markschemeJa: System AのNUEを105÷190×100≈55.3%、surplusを85 kg N/haと計算する。
System BのNUEを92÷135×100≈68.1%、surplusを43 kg N/haと計算する。
BはyieldがAより0.5 t/ha低いだけだが、N efficiencyが高くsurplusが大幅に小さいと比較する。
soil organic matter trendからBがlong-term soil conditionにも有利な可能性を示し、他inputやmanagementが不明であることも認識する。
大きなN surplusがnitrate leaching/eutrophication、ammonia loss、nitrous oxide emission、soil/water degradationなどにつながると説明する。
modelAnswer: System A has an NUE of about 55.3% and a nitrogen surplus of 85 kg N ha⁻¹. System B has an NUE of about 68.1% and a surplus of 43 kg N ha⁻¹. B therefore uses nitrogen more efficiently while producing only slightly less yield, and its soil-organic-matter trend is more favorable. A large nitrogen surplus can be lost by leaching or runoff, contributing to eutrophication, or can be emitted as nitrogen gases including nitrous oxide.
modelAnswerJa: System AのNUEは約55.3%、N surplusは85 kg N/haです。System Bは約68.1%、surplus 43 kg N/haです。Bはyieldが少し低いだけでNをより効率的に使い、soil organic matter trendも良好です。大きなN surplusはleachingやrunoffで失われeutrophicationにつながったり、nitrous oxideなどのgasとして排出されたりします。

subject: ESS HL

stimulus.title: Annual greenhouse-gas mitigation options
stimulus.description: Hypothetical modeled values for four measures.
stimulus.note: Average abatement cost = annual net cost / annual reduction. Other co-benefits are not monetized.

question: Calculate the average abatement cost for each measure and evaluate which two-measure combination appears most cost-effective if at least 18 Mt CO₂e yr⁻¹ of reduction is required. State one limitation of using abatement cost alone.
markscheme: Calculates average abatement costs as efficiency = US$15/t CO₂e, methane capture = US$8/t, electric buses = US$25/t, and reforestation = US$9/t.
Identifies methane capture + reforestation as providing exactly 18 Mt CO₂e yr⁻¹ at a combined annual cost of US$154 million.
Compares feasible alternatives and recognizes that methane capture + reforestation has the lowest combined cost among combinations meeting at least 18 Mt CO₂e yr⁻¹ in the table.
Evaluates that cost-effectiveness supports this pair but practical constraints such as land competition and gas-collection infrastructure must also be considered.
States one limitation such as omission of health, biodiversity, employment or energy-security co-benefits, uncertainty in modeled reductions, distributional effects, or different project lifetimes.
markschemeJa: average abatement costをefficiency=US$15/t CO₂e、methane capture=US$8/t、electric bus=US$25/t、reforestation=US$9/tと計算する。
methane capture＋reforestationが18 Mt CO₂e/yrをちょうど満たし、combined annual costがUS$154 millionと示す。
18 Mt以上を満たす他のcombinationと比較し、このpairが表内で最も低costと認識する。
cost-effectiveness上は有利だが、land competitionやgas-collection infrastructureなどimplementation constraintも考慮すべきと評価する。
health/biodiversity/employment/energy-security co-benefit、省略されたuncertainty、distributional effect、project lifetime差などcostだけのlimitを述べる。
modelAnswer: Average abatement costs are US$15/t for building efficiency, US$8/t for methane capture, US$25/t for electric buses and US$9/t for reforestation. Methane capture plus reforestation gives the required 18 Mt CO₂e reduction at US$154 million per year, which is the cheapest qualifying pair. It is therefore the most cost-effective combination in the table, but land competition and infrastructure still matter, and abatement cost alone ignores many co-benefits and social effects.
modelAnswerJa: average abatement costはbuilding efficiency 15、methane capture 8、electric bus 25、reforestation 9 US$/t CO₂eです。methane capture＋reforestationは18 Mt CO₂e reductionを満たしannual costはUS$154 millionで、条件を満たすpairの中で最も低costです。ただしland competitionやinfrastructureも重要で、abatement costだけではco-benefitやsocial effectを評価できません。

subject: ESS HL

stimulus.title: Urban heat-adaptation pilot projects
stimulus.description: Hypothetical measured outcomes during hot summer days.
stimulus.note: Effects vary with location, building design and maintenance.

question: Compare the interventions and evaluate why a city might use a combination rather than a single heat-adaptation measure.
markscheme: Uses the data to show that street trees have the largest listed surface-temperature reduction, while cool roofs are the lowest-cost option.
Recognizes that green roofs provide the strongest storm-water retention and additional habitat benefits but have the highest cost index.
Explains that the measures act through different mechanisms and locations, so combining them can reduce heat while also improving storm-water management, habitat and/or building energy performance.
Evaluates that a portfolio can improve urban resilience but effectiveness depends on local space, building suitability, maintenance, water availability and equitable access to benefits.
markschemeJa: dataからstreet treesのsurface-temperature reductionが最大で、cool roofsは最もlow-costと示す。
green roofsはstorm-water retentionが最も高くhabitat benefitもあるがcost indexも最大と認識する。
各measureは異なるmechanism/locationで働くため、組み合わせることでheat reductionに加えstorm-water、habitat、building energyにもbenefitを得られると説明する。
portfolioはurban resilienceを高め得るが、space、building suitability、maintenance、water availability、公平なbenefit accessに依存すると評価する。
modelAnswer: Street trees show the largest surface cooling, cool roofs are cheapest, and green roofs provide the strongest storm-water retention. Because the measures work in different parts of the urban system, a mix can reduce heat while also lowering cooling demand, improving runoff control and supporting habitat. A portfolio is therefore more resilient than one measure alone, but local space, maintenance, water demand and equitable access must be considered.
modelAnswerJa: street treesはsurface coolingが最大、cool roofsは最も低cost、green roofsはstorm-water retentionが最大です。異なるurban systemの部分に作用するため、組み合わせることでheat reductionに加えcooling demand低下、runoff control、habitat supportも得られます。したがってportfolioの方がresilientですが、space、maintenance、water demand、公平性を考慮する必要があります。

subject: ESS HL

stimulus.title: Aluminium material flow in an appliance industry
stimulus.note: Assume unaccounted material is process loss. Recycled metal can substitute for some primary aluminium input.

question: Calculate (i) manufacturing process loss, (ii) end-of-life collection rate relative to aluminium in products sold, and (iii) recycling yield from collected aluminium. Analyse how increasing circularity could reduce pressure on primary resources.
markscheme: Calculates process loss as 500 - 60 - 410 = 30 thousand t yr⁻¹.
Calculates end-of-life collection rate as 250 / 410 × 100 ≈ 61.0%.
Calculates recycling yield from collected aluminium as 210 / 250 × 100 = 84.0%.
Recognizes that improved collection, product design, repair/reuse and higher recycling yield can return more aluminium to production and reduce demand for primary extraction.
Analyses that circularity can reduce mining, waste and some energy use, while recognizing that recycling has losses and cannot eliminate primary demand if total material demand grows.
markschemeJa: process lossを500−60−410＝30 thousand t/yrと計算する。
end-of-life collection rateを250÷410×100≈61.0%と計算する。
collected aluminiumからのrecycling yieldを210÷250×100＝84.0%と計算する。
collection、product design、repair/reuse、recycling yield改善によってproductionへ戻るaluminiumを増やしprimary extraction demandを下げられると認識する。
circularityはmining、waste、一部energy useを減らし得るが、recycling lossがありtotal demandが増えればprimary demandを完全にはなくせないと分析する。
modelAnswer: Manufacturing process loss is 30 thousand tonnes per year. The end-of-life collection rate is about 61.0%, and 84.0% of collected aluminium is successfully recycled. Better collection, longer product life, repair, reuse and more efficient recycling would return more metal to production and reduce demand for newly mined aluminium. However, recycling is never loss-free and continued growth in total material demand can still require primary extraction.
modelAnswerJa: manufacturing process lossは30 thousand t/yrです。end-of-life collection rateは約61.0%、collected aluminiumのrecycling yieldは84.0%です。collection改善、product life延長、repair/reuse、efficient recyclingによりproductionへ戻るmetalを増やし、新規mining demandを減らせます。ただしrecyclingにはlossがあり、total demandが増え続ければprimary extractionは残ります。

subject: ESS HL

stimulus.title: Life-cycle emissions from three electricity options
stimulus.description: Hypothetical planning values for new generation projects.
stimulus.note: 1 GWh = 1,000,000 kWh. Values are illustrative and exclude transmission expansion.

question: Calculate the annual life-cycle greenhouse-gas emissions for wind and gas in tonnes CO₂e, compare them, and explain one energy-system trade-off relevant to replacing gas with wind and solar.
markscheme: Calculates wind emissions as 1800 × 1,000,000 × 14 g = 25,200 t CO₂e yr⁻¹.
Calculates gas emissions as 1900 × 1,000,000 × 430 g = 817,000 t CO₂e yr⁻¹.
Recognizes that gas has about 32 times the annual life-cycle emissions of the wind project in the stated data.
Explains that wind and solar can greatly reduce greenhouse-gas emissions but their variable output may require storage, demand response, interconnection or other firm capacity.
Recognizes that gas is dispatchable and can support reliability but creates much higher emissions and may expose the system to fuel-price or import risks.
markschemeJa: wind emissionsを1800×1,000,000×14 g＝25,200 t CO₂e/yrと計算する。
gas emissionsを1900×1,000,000×430 g＝817,000 t CO₂e/yrと計算する。
示されたdataではgasのannual life-cycle emissionがwindの約32倍と認識する。
wind/solarはGHGを大幅に減らせるがvariable outputのためstorage、demand response、interconnection、firm capacityなどが必要になり得ると説明する。
gasはdispatchableでreliabilityに寄与する一方、emissionsが高くfuel-price/import riskもあり得ると認識する。
modelAnswer: Wind produces about 25,200 t CO₂e per year, while gas produces about 817,000 t CO₂e per year, roughly 32 times more in this example. Replacing gas generation with wind and solar can sharply reduce emissions, but variable renewable output does not always match demand, so storage, demand response, transmission or other firm capacity may be needed. Gas offers dispatchability but at a much larger climate cost.
modelAnswerJa: windは約25,200 t CO₂e/yr、gasは約817,000 t CO₂e/yrで、この例ではgasが約32倍です。gasをwind/solarへ置き換えるとemissionを大幅に減らせますが、variable outputは需要と常に一致しないためstorage、demand response、transmission、firm capacityなどが必要です。gasはdispatchableですがclimate costが大きいです。

subject: ESS HL

stimulus.title: Demographic and consumption indicators for two countries
stimulus.note: Environmental impact depends on technology, energy source, inequality and many other factors not shown.

question: Calculate the approximate annual increase in population for each country and compare how demographic structure and per-capita consumption could produce different types of environmental pressure.
markscheme: Calculates Country A annual population increase as 18 million × 0.2% = 0.036 million, or about 36,000 people.
Calculates Country B annual population increase as 92 million × 1.8% = 1.656 million, or about 1.66 million people.
Uses the high under-15 share and growth rate in B to infer greater future demand for housing, food, water, schools, jobs and infrastructure if the population continues to grow.
Uses the much higher per-capita electricity use in A to recognize that lower population growth does not necessarily mean low environmental pressure because consumption per person can be high.
Concludes that population size/growth and per-capita consumption interact, while noting that energy mix, technology, inequality and policy affect actual environmental impact.
markschemeJa: Country Aのannual population increaseを18 million×0.2%=0.036 million、約36,000人と計算する。
Country Bを92 million×1.8%=1.656 million、約1.66 million人と計算する。
Bの高いunder-15 shareとgrowth rateから、population growthが続けばhousing、food、water、school、job、infrastructure demandが増えると推論する。
Aはpopulation growthが低くてもper-capita electricity useが大幅に高く、1人当たりconsumptionが高ければenvironmental pressureが大きくなり得ると認識する。
population size/growthとper-capita consumptionが相互作用し、energy mix、technology、inequality、policyもactual impactを左右すると結論づける。
modelAnswer: Country A adds about 36,000 people per year, while Country B adds about 1.66 million. B's rapid growth and large young population imply strong future demand for basic services and infrastructure. However, A uses five times as much electricity per person, showing that slow population growth can still be associated with high resource and energy pressure. Environmental impact therefore depends on both demographic change and consumption patterns, as well as technology and energy source.
modelAnswerJa: Country Aは年間約36,000人、Country Bは約1.66 million人増えます。Bはgrowthが速くyoung populationも大きいため、basic serviceやinfrastructure demandが強く増える可能性があります。一方Aはper-capita electricity useが5倍で、slow growthでもresource/energy pressureが高くなり得ます。したがってenvironmental impactはdemographyとconsumption patternの両方、さらにtechnologyやenergy sourceに依存します。

subject: ESS HL

stimulus.title: Proposed road project through semi-natural grassland
stimulus.description: Hypothetical planning information for a development approval.
rows: Restore 180 ha of degraded grassland elsewhere
Offset must be monitored for 20 years
Road reduces freight costs by an estimated US$24 million yr⁻¹
Local residents value the original site for access, heritage and rare species
stimulus.note: The ecological equivalence and long-term success of restoration are uncertain.

question: Evaluate the proposed biodiversity offset using environmental law, environmental economics and environmental ethics. Reach a justified conclusion.
markscheme: Applies environmental law by recognizing that enforceable conditions, monitoring, additionality, long-term responsibility and compliance mechanisms are necessary if an offset is permitted.

Applies environmental economics by comparing development benefits with environmental externalities and recognizing that restoration or compensation attempts to internalize some biodiversity costs but may not capture all ecosystem-service or non-market values.

Applies environmental ethics by considering intrinsic value of the original habitat, place-based/community values, environmental justice and/or whether biodiversity at one location is morally interchangeable with habitat elsewhere.
Evaluates ecological uncertainty: restoring 180 ha does not guarantee equivalence because quality, time lags, rare species, connectivity and restoration failure matter.

Reaches a justified conditional conclusion, for example that the offset should not substitute for avoid/minimize measures unless residual impacts are genuinely unavoidable and the offset is enforceable, additional and likely to achieve comparable ecological outcomes.
markschemeJa: environmental lawとして、offsetを認めるならenforceable condition、monitoring、additionality、long-term responsibility、compliance mechanismが必要と認識する。
environmental economicsとしてdevelopment benefitとenvironmental externalityを比較し、restoration/compensationは一部costをinternalizeするがecosystem serviceやnon-market valueを完全には表せないと認識する。
environmental ethicsとしてoriginal habitatのintrinsic value、place-based/community value、environmental justice、別の場所のhabitatで代替可能かを考慮する。
180 haをrestoreしてもquality、time lag、rare species、connectivity、restoration failureによりecological equivalenceが保証されないと評価する。
avoid/minimizeで残るimpactが本当にunavoidableで、offsetがenforceable・additional・comparable outcomeを達成する可能性が高い場合に限る等、根拠あるconditional conclusionを示す。
modelAnswer: The offset has potential value but should not be treated as automatically equivalent to the 120 ha lost. Legally, the approval would need enforceable restoration targets, independent monitoring and responsibility for failure. Economically, the road creates large freight benefits, but habitat loss is an external cost and many ecological and cultural values are not fully captured by money. Ethically, rare species, intrinsic habitat value and the community's attachment to the original site matter. Because restoration quality, time lags and ecological equivalence are uncertain, the road should first avoid and minimize damage; an offset should address only genuinely residual impacts and should proceed only with strong, additional and enforceable safeguards.
